# CADSysFNC — changes for Masterplanner

**Library:** `Documents\development\delphi_libraries\CADSysFNC` (OwlHatSoftware/CADSysFNC; masters in `Sources\VCL.*`, per-framework units generated by `Tools\gen-units.cmd`)
**Reviewed version:** commit `1c81661` ("Docs: drawing speed")
**Framework used by Masterplanner:** **FMX** (`Generated\FMX`)
**Requirement links:** Masterplanner Phase 1 requirements §7 (bar rendering), §8.1.1 (timescale design), §10.3 / §10.3a (output, model space and paper views), MP-NFR-102/103; implementation plan WP-0.1, WP-0.2, WP-3.x, WP-5.x

Priorities: **Must** = needed for Masterplanner P1.0; **Should** = P1.0 if possible, else P1.1; **Could** = later.

All changes go into `Sources\VCL.*` (the masters) and are regenerated for FMX/VCL/LCL. Each one keeps existing drawings, JSON files and VisualPlannerFNC working unchanged.

---

## 1. What CADSysFNC already gives Masterplanner (no change needed)

| Need | Already there |
|---|---|
| Model space with custom shapes | `TObject2D` / `TFrame2D` descendants, `CADSysRegisterClass`, JSON round-trip (as VisualPlanner's legend and date box) |
| Paper views with viewports at a scale | `TCADSheet`, `TCADSheetViewport` (`RectMM`, `View`, `UnitsPerMM`, `ShowBorder`), named views, viewport handles (`docs\paper-space.md`) |
| One renderer for screen, preview, print and PDF | `CADDrawSheet` / `CADDrawSheetViewports`, `CADSaveSheetsToPDF` (`TTMSFNCGraphicsPDFEngine`) |
| Line weights in mm on paper | `TCADPen.LineWeightMM`, `TCADGraphics.PixelsPerMM` |
| Alpha colours | `TCADColor` with alpha; FNC backend sets `Opacity` |
| Hatching | `TCADGraphics.HatchPolygon` (backend-independent) |
| Wrapped and rotated text | `DrawText` with `CAD_DT_WORDBREAK`; rotation via `TCADFontSpec.Escapement` in the FNC backend; `CAD_DT_CALCRECT` for measuring |
| Clipping | `PushClip` / `PopClip`, nested and intersected |
| Large drawings on screen | sub-pixel culling (`SmallObjectMode`), pan/zoom from the drawn picture (`docs\drawing-speed.md`) |
| A screen-only overlay | `TFNCCADViewport.OnPaintOverlay` — usable for a header that stays at the top of the window (requirements §8.1.1, later option) |

## 3. CS-01 — Viewport content inset and draw hook

**Problem.** `DrawSheetViewport` (in `VCL.FNCCADSys4.pas`) draws the model objects inside the viewport rectangle and then the border. An application cannot draw anything of its own **per viewport** — and a Gantt sheet needs a timescale header for exactly the date window that viewport shows, and a lane-header column for exactly its lanes. Drawing those as model objects does not work: they would be at the top/left of the model, not of each viewport.

**Change — inset.**

```pascal
TCADSheetViewport
  { : Margins inside RectMM, in mm of paper, that the model is NOT drawn
      in: Left, Top, Right, Bottom. Zero by default (today's behaviour).
      The model window is fitted to / scaled into RectMM minus the inset;
      the application draws its own furniture in the margins (CS-01 hook). }
  property ContentInsetMM: TRect2D;     // Left, Top, Right, Bottom stored as a rect of four widths
  function ContentRectMM: TRect2D;      // RectMM deflated by the inset
```

Everything that today uses `RectMM` to place, fit or invert the model uses `ContentRectMM` instead: `EffectiveUnitsPerMM` (fit), `ModelWindow`, `PointMMToModel`, `ModelToPointMM`, `CADSheetViewportTransform`, and the clip in `DrawSheetViewport`. `ViewportAt` / `ViewportIndexAt`, the border and the handles keep using `RectMM`.

**Change — hook.**

```pascal
type
  TCADViewportDrawPhase = (vdpBeforeModel, vdpAfterModel);

  TCADSheetViewportDrawInfo = record
    Sheet: TCADSheet;
    Viewport: TCADSheetViewport;
    Canvas: TDecorativeCanvas;
    Device: TCADPageDevice;
    OuterPx: TRect;            // RectMM in device pixels
    ContentPx: TRect;          // ContentRectMM in device pixels
    ModelToDevice: TTransf2D;  // the transform the model was drawn with
    ModelWindow: TRect2D;      // the part of the model shown, in world units
    PixelsPerMM: Double;       // of the device
    DrawMode: Cardinal;
  end;

  TCADSheetViewportDrawEvent = procedure(Sender: TObject;
    const AInfo: TCADSheetViewportDrawInfo;
    const APhase: TCADViewportDrawPhase) of object;

TFNCCADCmp2D
  property OnDrawSheetViewport: TCADSheetViewportDrawEvent;
```

`DrawSheetViewport` calls it twice: `vdpBeforeModel` (clip = `OuterPx`; e.g. a lane-band background) and `vdpAfterModel` (clip = `OuterPx`; headers, continuation marks), then draws the border last as today. Because the editing viewport, the preview, the printer and the PDF writer all come through `DrawSheetViewport`, the furniture appears identically everywhere.

The handler must leave the canvas state as it found it; `DrawSheetViewport` wraps the call in `SaveState`/`RestoreState` and a `PushClip`/`PopClip` pair so a careless handler cannot leak a clip (on FMX a leaked clip is fatal, as `ClipDepth`'s comment notes).

**Test:** a sheet with two viewports onto different windows of one model; the hook draws the window's x-range as text in the top inset of each; preview, PDF and editing viewport show the same; the fit with an inset leaves the inset empty of model; `PointMMToModel` inside the content rect maps correctly.

## 4. CS-02 — Application data on a viewport

```pascal
TCADSheetViewport
  { : Opaque text owned by the application (typically JSON), saved and
      loaded with the viewport, copied by Assign, never interpreted by the
      library. Empty by default and then not written to the file. }
  property AppData: String;
```

JSON key `"appData"` (string), written only when not empty. Masterplanner stores per viewport: lane range, date window, which headers to draw, page-series membership. (A side table keyed by viewport `Name` would also work, but names are not unique and do not survive copy/paste of a sheet.)

The same property on `TCADSheet` (`"appData"`) for sheet-level data (sheet number in a series, the series' split rule) — **Should**.

---

## 5. CS-03 — Linear gradient brush

**Problem.** `TCADBrushStyle` has solid, clear and the six hatch styles; there is no gradient, and the reference plates use shaded bars.

**Change.**

```pascal
TCADBrush
  property Color2: TCADColor;              // gradient end colour
  property GradientVertical: Boolean;      // False: left→right, True: top→bottom
TCADBrushStyle = (..., cbsGradient);       // appended, so stored ordinals do not move
```

- `TCADSimpleBrush` stores the two new values; `Assign` copies them; layer brushes are saved with `"color2"` and `"gradientVertical"` only when the style is `cbsGradient`.
- **FNC backend** (`VCL.FNCCS4GraphicsFNC`): `Fill.Kind := gfkGradient`, `Fill.Color := Color`, `Fill.ColorTo := Color2`, `Fill.Orientation := gfoHorizontal / gfoVertical`, opacity from the alpha of `Color`. This covers screen and PDF (the PDF engine is an FNC graphics).
- **VCL GDI backend** (`VCL.FNCCS4GraphicsVCL`): `GradientFill` for rectangles; polygons clipped with a region and filled by `GradientFill` over their bounding box; or, minimum, the average colour.
- **SVG backend** (CS-05): `<linearGradient>` in `<defs>`.
- **GDI/EMF backend** (CS-06): as the VCL GDI backend.
- Hatching is unaffected (`Hatching` stays false for `cbsGradient`).

Arbitrary angles are not needed (bars are horizontal); keep to the two orientations FNC supports.

## 6. CS-04 — Image export

```pascal
{ VCL.FNCCS4Print (or a new VCL.FNCCS4Image) — all frameworks }
procedure CADSaveSheetToImage(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ASheet: TCADSheet;
  const AFileName: String; const ADPI: Integer = 300;
  const ATransparent: Boolean = False);
procedure CADSaveModelRectToImage(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ARect: TRect2D;
  const AUnitsPerMM: TRealType; const AFileName: String;
  const ADPI: Integer = 300; const ATransparent: Boolean = False);
```

Implementation: a `TTMSFNCBitmap` sized from the sheet (mm × DPI / 25.4), an FNC graphics on it, a `TCADPageDevice` with `PixelsPerMM = DPI / 25.4`, then `CADDrawSheet` (or the page routine for a model rectangle); save as PNG. `ATransparent` skips the background fill. Guard the bitmap size (an A0 sheet at 600 dpi is ~19,900 × 28,100 px): fall back to tiling into strips or refuse with a message above a configurable pixel limit.

---

## 7. CS-05 — SVG backend

New unit `VCL.FNCCS4SVG` (framework-free; generated for all three):

```pascal
type
  TCADSVGGraphics = class(TCADGraphics)   // writes SVG elements into a string builder
  public
    constructor Create(const AWidthPx, AHeightPx: Integer; const APixelsPerMM: Double);
    function SVGText: String;             // the complete document
  end;

procedure CADSaveSheetsToSVG(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ASheets: array of TCADSheet;
  const AFileNamePattern: String);        // e.g. 'plate-%d.svg', one file per sheet
procedure CADSaveSheetToSVGStream(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ASheet: TCADSheet;
  const AStream: TStream);
```

Mapping of the abstract `TCADGraphics` calls:

| Call | SVG |
|---|---|
| `MoveTo`/`LineTo`/`Polyline` | `<polyline>` (consecutive `LineTo`s merged) |
| `DoPolygon`, `DoRectangle`, `DoEllipse`, `DoFillRect` | `<polygon>`, `<rect>`, `<ellipse>` with `fill`/`stroke` |
| pen | `stroke`, `stroke-width` (mm × PixelsPerMM), `stroke-dasharray` per `TCADPenStyle`, `stroke-opacity` |
| brush | `fill`, `fill-opacity`; `cbsGradient` → `<linearGradient>`; hatch styles never arrive (the base class draws them as lines) |
| `SelectFont` / `DrawText` | `<text>` with `font-family`, `font-size`, weight/style; rotation as `transform="rotate(...)"`; **word wrap is laid out by the backend** (SVG has none): measure with a hidden FNC graphics (`CalculateText`) word by word and emit one `<tspan>` per line; `CAD_DT_CALCRECT` answered by the same measurer |
| `DrawImage` | `<image href="data:image/png;base64,...">` from `TCADImage` bytes |
| `PushClip`/`PopClip` | `<clipPath>` + `<g clip-path="...">` |

Coordinates are written in device units of a 600 dpi layout with a `viewBox` in mm, so the file has the sheet's real size and keeps the precision the PDF writer gets (see the comment in `VCL.FNCCS4PDF`).

## 8. CS-06 — EMF and clipboard on FMX (Windows)

**Problem.** Clipboard copy exists only in `VCL.FNCCS4ExportVCL` (it needs a VCL `TCanvas`/`TClipboard`). An FMX application has no way to put a vector picture on the clipboard for Word or PowerPoint.

**Change.** New unit `VCL.FNCCS4GDI` (Windows-only, **no VCL dependency**, generated for VCL and FMX):

```pascal
type
  { : A TCADGraphics on a raw GDI device context (HDC): MoveToEx/LineTo,
      Polyline, Polygon, Rectangle, Ellipse, ExtCreatePen, CreateBrushIndirect,
      CreateFontIndirectW with lfEscapement, DrawTextW (word break, calc rect),
      IntersectClipRect/SaveDC/RestoreDC. Alpha is flattened against
      BlendBackground (GDI has none). Gradients via GradientFill. }
  TCADGDIGraphics = class(TCADGraphics)
  public
    constructor Create(const ADC: HDC; const APixelsPerMM: Double);
  end;

{ An enhanced metafile of a sheet (or a model rectangle) at full quality. }
function  CADSheetToEMF(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ASheet: TCADSheet;
  const ADPI: Integer = 600): HENHMETAFILE;
procedure CADSaveSheetToEMF(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ASheet: TCADSheet;
  const AFileName: String);
{ Puts CF_ENHMETAFILE and a PNG ("PNG" registered format) + CF_DIB on the
  Windows clipboard, so Office pastes the vector picture and other programs
  the bitmap. }
procedure CADCopySheetToClipboardWin(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ASheet: TCADSheet);
procedure CADCopyModelRectToClipboardWin(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ARect: TRect2D;
  const AUnitsPerMM: TRealType);
```

The metafile is recorded with `CreateEnhMetaFileW` on a reference DC, sized in 0.01 mm from the sheet, drawn through `CADDrawSheet` with a `TCADGDIGraphics`. Optionally (Could) the VCL backend `VCL.FNCCS4GraphicsVCL` can later sit on `TCADGDIGraphics` instead of its own copy of the GDI calls.

## 9. CS-07 — Printing on FMX

`CADPrintPages` / `CADPrintSheets` live in `VCL.FNCCS4ExportVCL` (VCL `TPrinter`). For FMX add, in a new unit `VCL.FNCCS4PrintFMX` (generated for FMX only):

```pascal
function  CADFMXPrinterPageDevice: TCADPageDevice;      // from FMX.Printer: size, DPI, printable area
procedure CADPrintSheetsFMX(const ACAD: TFNCCADCmp2D; const ASheets: TCADSheets;
  const ATitle: String);
```

Drawing through an FNC graphics on `Printer.Canvas` per page, using `CADDrawSheet` like the VCL version. **Fallback** already used by VisualPlannerFNC (write a temporary PDF and hand it to the shell's `print` verb) stays acceptable if FMX printer output proves unreliable; then this item is closed with a documented decision.

---

**Done as:** not through the FMX printer canvas but through GDI on the active FMX printer's own device context - `VCL.FNCCS4PrintFMX` (`CADPrintSheetsFMX`, `CADPrintPagesFMX`, `CADFMXPrinterPageDevice`) over `CADPrintSheetsWin` / `CADPrintPagesWin` in `VCL.FNCCS4GDI`. Same drawing as the EMF and the VCL print, and each sheet sets its own orientation and (standard) paper by resetting the DC between pages. Copies and other settings made on FMX's printer object are not carried over. Windows only; elsewhere the calls raise `ECADPageError` and the PDF is the way to paper.

## 10. CS-08 — PDF: links and fonts

- **Links:** an optional list of link areas passed to `CADSaveSheetsToPDF` (or a callback per sheet): `TCADPDFLink = record RectMM: TRect2D; URL: String; end;` → link annotations on the page. Use the URL/link support of `TTMSFNCPDFLib` if FNC Core provides it; if it does not, record that as a known limitation in `VCL.FNCCS4PDF`'s header comment and close the item.
- **Fonts:** expose whether TrueType fonts are embedded (and subset) — a global `CADPDFEmbedFonts: Boolean = True` passed to the FNC PDF library — and document what happens with a font that is not installed.

---

**Done as:** `CADSaveSheetsToPDF` takes an optional `TCADPDFSheetLinksFunc` returning `TCADPDFLink` records per sheet. FNC only links over text it draws (`AddURL`) and its rectangle-taking routine is out of reach in an implementation section, so the links are appended after writing as a PDF incremental update (`CADAddPDFLinks`, public). `CADPDFEmbedFonts` (default True) and `CADPDFFontFallbacks` (tried in order for a font that is not installed; with none of them available the name is written unembedded and the reader substitutes) are set on the FNC PDF library when a document starts. See the `VCL.FNCCS4PDF` header.

## 11. CS-09 — Anisotropic viewport scale (Could, P1.1)

```pascal
TCADSheetViewport
  { : Drawing units per mm vertically; 0 = same as UnitsPerMM (today). }
  property UnitsPerMMY: TRealType;
```

Lets a sheet show ten years of a plate across an A3 width while lanes keep their height. Affects `EffectiveUnitsPerMM` (fit per axis), `ModelWindow`, `PointMMToModel`/`ModelToPointMM`, `CADSheetViewportTransform`, JSON (`"unitsPerMMY"`, written only when set). Library text shapes would be stretched; Masterplanner's own shapes size their text in device units and are not affected. Document that limitation.

## 12. CS-10 — Verification items (expected to work; confirm in the Masterplanner spike WP-0.1)

| Item | How to check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Rotated text (`Escapement`) in PDF and SVG at the right position | a 45° label anchored at a milestone, screen vs PDF vs SVG | fix the rotation origin in the backend |
| Word-wrapped text with `CAD_DT_CALCRECT` matches what `DrawText` draws, at 600 dpi | measure, draw, compare line count | align measure and draw in the FNC backend |
| Dash styles scale with `LineWeightMM` on paper | dashed 0.5 mm line in PDF | scale dash pattern by pen width |
| Polygons with ~40 points per rounded end (rounded bars, arrow caps) look smooth in PDF | zoom the PDF | none expected (600 dpi layout) |
| 5,000 custom shapes: redraw and `PickObject` on FMX | existing benchmark with Masterplanner shapes | consider a spatial index for picking |
| `OnPaintOverlay` gives access to the canvas and the current transform | draw a header band in the overlay | expose them |

---

**Checked on the library side (2026-10-16):**

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Rotated text in PDF and SVG | **Fixed where it disagreed.** The rule is FNC's own, as its PDF engine applies it (checked by rasterising a PDF of eight layouts): the text is laid out level in the bounding box of its rectangle once turned, then turned about the rectangle's middle - `CADRotatedTextRect`. The SVG laid it out in the rectangle itself, and GDI (the EMF, printing through `VCL.FNCCS4GDI` and through a VCL `TCanvas`) turned each line about its start, about 20 px out at 45 degrees; all three now follow the rule. **Known deviation:** FNC's GDI+ context - the VCL screen and the VCL PNG - displaces turned text across the line by an amount that grows with the rectangle's height (28 px for a 40 px rectangle at 45 degrees). Turning it ourselves through `TTMSFNCGraphics.SetMatrix` does not work: GDI+ text ignores that matrix. Masterplanner is FMX, whose context uses the same formula as the PDF engine; to be confirmed by eye in the spike. Worth reporting to TMS. |
| Word wrap: `CAD_DT_CALCRECT` against `DrawText` at 600 dpi | Agrees on the FNC backend; test `WrappedTextIsAsTallAsItWasMeasured`. The SVG measures through the same FNC call. |
| Dashes on paper | **Fixed.** FNC's PDF writer puts a fixed `[4] 1 d` on a dashed stroke, in page units - at 600 dpi a sixth of a millimetre, so a dashed line printed solid. The PDF backend now draws dashed pens as solid pieces from `CADDashPattern`, the pattern the SVG and the EMF use, which scales with the pen's width (a hairline dashes 4.8 mm on, 1.6 mm off; checked by rasterising). |
| Polygons with many points in a PDF | Nothing to do: 600 dpi layout. |
| 5,000 shapes on FMX | For the spike, with Masterplanner's shapes. For scale: `docs\drawing-speed.md` (100,000 lines, FMX repaint at zoom-all 209 ms). |
| `OnPaintOverlay` | Nothing to expose: the event's `Sender` is the viewport, whose public `OnScreenCanvas` and `ViewportToScreenTransform` are the canvas and the transform. On FMX the overlay canvas carries a `ViewScale` matrix. |
| *Found on the way:* text size in a PDF on the VCL | **Fixed.** FNC's PDF engine takes the font's `Size`, which on the VCL is the pixel height turned into points at the font's pixels per inch - three quarters of the intended size at 96 dpi, under a third at 240. `TCADPDFGraphics.SelectFont` now sets the size to the pixel height. A 10 mm text object now has 6.3 mm capitals, as it should. FMX was not affected. **VCL PDFs written before this have text 25% too small.** |

**Results (WP-0.1, 2026-10-16):** rotated text — SVG ✅, PDF ❌ → CS-13, screen/PNG clipped → CS-15; `CAD_DT_CALCRECT` vs `DrawText` ✅; dashes — PNG/SVG ✅, PDF ❌ → CS-14; rounded polygons in PDF ✅; 5,000 shapes — redraw ≈ 0.05 ms per visible shape, picking 0.1 ms over 8,202 objects (no spatial index needed for picking); `OnPaintOverlay` not tested.

## 14. CS-12 — PDF: gradient fills (Must)

**Found in WP-0.1.** At `CADPDFResolution = 600` a polygon or rectangle filled with `cbsGradient` is not drawn at all; with `CADPDFResolution = 72` the same page renders the gradient correctly. The brush is right (screen, PNG and SVG show it), so the gradient reaches `TTMSFNCGraphicsPDFEngine`, whose shading is set up in coordinates the 600 dpi → points page transform does not apply to (the same class of unit mix as the page-height problem the unit header describes) — the shading ends up off the page or degenerate, and the fill with it.

**Status at `c1aabac`: open** — unchanged; the gradient-filled bar on sheet 2 of the spike's `spike.pdf` is not drawn, and is drawn correctly in `spike-72dpi.pdf`.

**Fix plan**, in order of preference:

1. In `TCADPDFGraphics`, convert the gradient's start and end points to what the PDF engine expects (multiply by `72 / CADPDFResolution`, or apply the inverse of the page transform) before handing the fill over. Check against the PDF engine's source which coordinates its shading uses.
2. If the engine cannot be fed correctly: draw a `cbsGradient` fill in the PDF backend as **N solid bands** (e.g. 32) clipped to the shape (`PushClip` to the polygon's box plus the polygon itself as a clip path), interpolating `Color` → `Color2`. Indistinguishable from a real gradient on paper, works in every backend, a few dozen more operators per shape.
3. Never silently drop the shape: if neither works, fill with the average of the two colours.

**Test:** a page with a horizontal and a vertical gradient rectangle and a gradient polygon at 600 dpi; parse the content stream for a shading (`sh`) or the band fills, and render the page (pdftoppm in the test suite or a stored reference image).

**Done as (`df6b798`):** fix plan 2. `TCADPDFGraphics` paints a `cbsGradient` fill as bands of solid colour - one per step of the channel that changes most, at most 256, never thinner than a dot - inside the shape's own outline as a clip path (`W n`), then strokes the outline with nothing to fill. Opaque bands overlap by a dot so a reader shows no seams. Plan 1 was not possible: FNC writes the pattern itself, with the shape's box in dots, no `/Matrix` and `/Extend[false false]`, from a routine in its implementation section. Rectangles, polygons, ellipses and `FillRect` all go this way. Test: `TCADPDFPaperTests.AGradientIsPaintedInBandsInsideItsShape`.

## 15. CS-13 — PDF: rotated text (Must)

**Found in WP-0.1.** At 600 dpi, text drawn with `Escapement` ≠ 0 is missing from the PDF (no rotated text matrix in the content stream); at 72 dpi it is there, in the right place. Lane captions (90°) and milestone labels (45°) depend on it.

**Status at `c1aabac`: open.** Turned text is now drawn, but misplaced at 600 dpi. `pdftotext -bbox` on the spike's `spike.pdf`: the 90° lane caption "Nieuwbouw ZS Reijerswaard" should sit in the lane column at the left edge (x ≈ 30–45 pt, as in `spike-72dpi.pdf`, where it is right); at 600 dpi only the word "Nieuwbouw" is found, mid-page at x 722–741, y 459–463 pt on sheet 1 and at x 86–124, y 495–503 pt on sheet 3, and on sheet 2 none of the turned words (lane captions, 45° milestone labels "Concept P&ID beschikbaar", "Definitief P&ID beschikbaar") are on the page at all. So the rotation centre (or the translation that goes with the turn) still takes the dots-to-points conversion once too often or not at all — the same class of unit mix as the page height. A check at 72 dpi, or on a page where the text sits near the origin, will not show it; the spike's sheets will (`mpspike01.exe -out <folder>`, compare the two PDFs).

**Fix plan:** do the rotation in `TCADPDFGraphics.DrawText` rather than passing the angle to the FNC/PDF engine: save the graphics state, rotate the PDF graphics' transform about the centre of the text rectangle (in dots, so the page transform scales it with everything else), draw the text unrotated, restore. Equivalent: emit a `Tm` with the rotation matrix through the PDF library's lower-level text call.

**Test:** 0°, 45°, 90°, 270° labels anchored at known points; extract with `pdftotext -bbox` and compare positions with the SVG output.

**Done as (`df6b798`):** the fix plan. Cause: FNC's `SetTextAngle` translates to `MediaBox height - centre Y` - points minus dots - while the library flips everything else against the page height in dots. `TCADPDFGraphics.DrawText` now saves the state, rotates about the centre of the caller's rectangle in the page's own dotted space (the save routines set `PageHeight`), draws the text level in the box FNC would have used (`CADRotatedTextRect`) and restores. Drawn level, FNC cuts a line longer than its box short, where turned it lets it run on - a 90° label in a box sized for level text came out as "Mil" - so the box is opened out on the side the alignment grows towards and the text kept to one line. Test: `TCADPDFPaperTests.TurnedTextLandsWhereItIsAnchored` follows `q`/`cm`/`Td`/`Tj` through the content stream: each label turned the right way, complete, within half a label of its anchor and within 2 pt of the 72 dpi page.

## 16. CS-14 — PDF: dash patterns (Must)

**Found in WP-0.1.** At 600 dpi `cpsDash`/`cpsDot` lines come out as very dense hatching: the dash array is written in dots and then scaled by 72/600, so every dash is 8.3 × too short. At 72 dpi the dashes are right.

**Status at `c1aabac`: fixed.** `TCADPDFGraphics` draws dashed pens as solid pieces with a pattern that scales with the pen width (`CADDashPattern` / `CADDashSegments`); confirmed in the spike's 600 dpi PDF.

**Fix plan:** in `TCADPDFGraphics`, scale the dash array by `CADPDFResolution / 72` (or derive it from the pen width in points) before it reaches the PDF. Better still, make dash lengths a multiple of the line width on every backend, so a 0.5 mm dashed line looks the same in PNG, SVG and PDF (the SVG backend already writes `180,60` / `36,36` at 600 dpi, which is right).

**Test:** a 0.25 mm and a 0.5 mm dashed and dotted line; measure the dash lengths in the content stream.

## 17. CS-15 — FNC backend: rotated text clipped (Must)

**Found in WP-0.1.** `TCADFNCGraphics.DrawText` with an angle passes its rectangle to `TTMSFNCGraphics.DrawText`, which rotates the text about the rectangle's centre and then clips it to the **unrotated** rectangle — `CAD_DT_NOCLIP` is not honoured. A 90° caption in a rectangle sized for the horizontal text showed only its middle ("ZS I" of "Nieuwbouw ZS Reijerswaard").

**Fix plan:** when the angle is not zero, pass FNC a square of side `width + height` of the text, centred on the centre of the caller's rectangle (what the Masterplanner spike does in `MPDrawRotatedText`). The text's position is unchanged; only the clip goes away. Document that a rotated `DrawText` positions by the rectangle's centre.

**Test:** draw a 90° label in a narrow rectangle onto a bitmap and check pixels along the rotated text's length.

**Done as (`7b15de7`):** the fix plan, for one-line turned text too. `TCADFNCGraphics.DrawText` places a one-line turned label by the common rule (`CADRotatedTextRect`, aligned as asked, free to run past the box, turned about the rectangle's middle). On FMX it hands FNC a square about the line's middle with the line centred in it - so the alignment is kept, not only centred labels - and nothing is cut. On the VCL the library's FNC graphics use FNC's general context, which turns text by a rule that only suits right angles; there it is drawn with GDI, a level font and a world transform, as `VCL.FNCCS4GraphicsVCL` does. Wrapped turned text still goes to FNC as before. Tests: `AnFNCTurnedLabelIsTheLevelLabelTurned`, `ALongTurnedLabelIsDrawnWhole`. Not yet seen on FMX by eye; the spike will show it.

## 18. CS-16 — GDI/EMF backend: wrapped text not centred vertically (Must)

**Found in WP-0.2** (`docs\spikes\wp02-output-spike.md`). `TCADGDIGraphics.DrawText` passes the `CAD_DT_` flags straight to `DrawTextW`. GDI honours `DT_VCENTER` (and `DT_BOTTOM`) only together with `DT_SINGLELINE`, so every wrapped label in an EMF sits at the top of its rectangle; the FNC backend (screen, PNG, PDF) and SVG centre it. Seen identically in Windows GDI playback and in PowerPoint.

**Fix plan:** when `CAD_DT_WORDBREAK` is set with `CAD_DT_VCENTER` or `CAD_DT_BOTTOM`, measure with `DT_CALCRECT` on the same width, offset the rectangle's top by half (or all) of the spare height, and draw without the vertical flag. Same in the turned-text path and in the VCL GDI backend (`VCL.FNCCS4GraphicsVCL`), which has the same call.

**Test:** a two-line label in a tall rectangle, `VCENTER`: the text's bounding box (from `DT_CALCRECT`, or rasterised) centred within one pixel, on GDI, FNC and SVG alike.

**Done as (`7b15de7`):** the fix plan, in `VCL.FNCCS4GDI` and `VCL.FNCCS4GraphicsVCL` (`GDIDrawText`). One-line turned text on GDI now also runs past its box (`DT_NOCLIP`), as everywhere else. Test: `AWrappedLabelIsCentredOnEveryBackend` - GDI, the VCL canvas and FNC each within 6 px of the box's middle.

## 19. CS-17 — EMF: uneven glyph spacing, text overflow (Must)

**Found in WP-0.2.** `CADSheetToEMF` records against the screen DC (`GetDC(0)`) with the sheet laid out at 600 dpi. Glyph advances are stored rounded at small font sizes, so on playback (Windows and PowerPoint alike) words show gaps ("Realisatieco ntract") and text that measured as fitting is wider than its box ("Opstellen vraagspecificati…" instead of wrapping). The **same sheet recorded at 2400 dpi** wraps and spaces correctly (`sheet-2-2400dpi.emf` in the spike's output).

**Fix plan:** make 2400 dpi (or higher) the default layout resolution for `CADSheetToEMF`, `CADModelRectToEMF` and the clipboard — the metafile is vector, so the file grows only by the larger numbers. Alternatively record against a high-resolution reference (a printer-like DC) or in `MM_HIMETRIC` logical units. Check that line weights and dash patterns (which scale with the pen) stay right at the new resolution.

**Test:** a paragraph that just fits a box, recorded and played back (`PlayEnhMetaFile` into a bitmap): same line breaks as the measure, no glyph gaps beyond a pixel.

**Done as (`7b15de7`):** `CADEMFResolution` (2400) is the layout resolution whenever `ADPI` is 0, now the default of `CADSheetToEMF`, `CADModelRectToEMF` and `CADSaveSheetToEMF`; the clipboard uses it. Line weights, dashes and hatching scale with it (they are in millimetres or scale with the pen); a one-pixel pen stays a cosmetic hairline. Test: `AMetafileSpacesSmallTextAsItMeasuredIt` reads the `EMR_EXTTEXTOUTW` dx arrays of 2.5 mm text - about 96 units a glyph by default, 24 at 600 dpi - and asks for at least 50, so the rounding stays under a percent. Playback widths at 300 dpi came out equal at 600, 2400 and 9600 dpi on the build machine, so the playback test the brief proposes could not tell them apart there.

## 20. CS-18 — SVG on the clipboard (Should)

**From WP-0.2 / decision 0002 (proposed).** PowerPoint 16 (Microsoft 365) renders the library's SVG more faithfully than its EMF. Put `CADSaveSheetToSVGStream`'s output on the clipboard under the registered format `image/svg+xml`, next to `CF_ENHMETAFILE`, PNG and `CF_DIB`, in `CADCopySheetToClipboardWin` and `CADCopyModelRectToClipboardWin`; programs take the best format they understand.

**Paste test (WP-0.2, 2026-10-17):** with EMF, PNG and DIB on the clipboard, a plain paste in PowerPoint and Word 16 takes the **PNG** — Office ranks PNG above `CF_ENHMETAFILE`; the metafile is only reachable through Paste Special. So, besides SVG: **do not put the registered `PNG` format on the clipboard together with the metafile** (or make it optional, default off); `CF_DIB` stays as the bitmap for programs without metafile support. Priority **Must** for that part, since without it MP-OUT-004's vector paste is not what users get.

**Test:** the clipboard holds all four formats after a copy; a manual paste into PowerPoint 365 gives the SVG.

**Done as (`7b15de7`):** both parts. The registered `PNG` is left off unless `CADClipboardPNG` (default False); `CF_DIB` stays. The SVG goes on under `image/svg+xml` while `CADClipboardSVG` (default True), for a sheet (`CADSaveSheetToSVGStream`) and for a model rectangle (drawn by `CADDrawModelRect` onto `TCADSVGGraphics`). Test: `TheClipboardHasTheMetafileTheSVGAndABitmap`. Pasted into PowerPoint by Jack from the spike's "Copy sheet (EMF)" on 2026-10-17: works.
